newsitem.title: USA: Coke Q1 worldwide unit case volume up.
newsitem.headline: Coke Q1 worldwide unit case volume up.

text.p: Coca-Cola Co said Monday that in the first quarter, worldwide unit case volume grew nine percent and gallon shipments of concentrates and syrups increased seven percent, both exceeding estimates.

This performance, the company said, results from continued investment in the marketplace and is paying off around the world, including sizable profitable growth in the company's most established market, the United States.
In the North America Group, the company said, first quarter unit case volume grew over eight percent, on top of a seven percent increase in the first quarter of 1996.
U.S. unit case volume growth was nine percent on top of an eight percent growth in the first quarter of 1996, the company said.
In the Greater Europe Group, the company said, first quarter unit case volume grew 11 percent, exceeding estimates, on top of a nine percent increase in the first quarter of 1996.
Unit case volume increased 26 percent in the East Central European Division, 15 percent in Italy and 18 percent in Spain in the first quarter, the company said.

Unit case volume in Germany declined two percent due to a difficult economic environment and challenging comparisons following eight percent unit case growth in the first quarter of 1996, the company said.
Gallon shipments increased 14 percent during the first quarter, the company said.
In the Latin America Group, first quarter unit case volume grew nine percent, the company said.
Unit case volume grew 15 percent in Chile, seven percent in Mexico and eight percent in Argentina, while decreasing one percent in Brazil, the company said.
Unit case volume and gallon shipments in Brazil were impacted by reduced consumer purchasing power and comparisons, although share continues to increase, the company said.
Gallon shipments for the Latin America Group were even in the first quarter, the company said.
In the Africa Group, first quarter unit case volume increased 10 percent, the company said.
Unit case volume rose eight percent in the Northern Africa Division and increased 11 percent in the Southern Africa Division, led by very strong growth in South Africa, the company said.
Gallon shipments increased 25 percent in the first quarter, the company said.
In the Middle and Far East Group, first quarter unit case volume increased eight percent, on top of a 14 percent increase in last year's first quarter, the company said.
Unit case volume grew 19 percent in China, six percent in Japan, and 15 percent in the Middle East Division, the company said.
Gallon shipments rose 12 percent in the first quarter.
At its Minute Maid Co unit, the company said first-quarter unit volume decreased seven percent, after a nine percent increase in the first quarter of 1996.
